title: Your Image in a Mirror
description: The crystal shard sits inside a mirror room. Umbra taunts: 'Reach for it and you'll grab only its image!' Learn exactly what a plane mirror image is really like.

content.value: When you stand in front of a flat (plane) mirror, you see an IMAGE of yourself. The image is not really behind the mirror — light only appears to come from there. Because you cannot catch this image on a screen, it is called a VIRTUAL image.
The 4 Rules of a Plane Mirror Image

1. VIRTUAL & ERECT   → upright, cannot be caught on a screen
2. SAME SIZE         → exactly as big as the object
3. SAME DISTANCE     → as far behind the mirror as you are in front
4. LATERALLY INVERTED → left and right appear swapped
If you stand 1 metre in front of a mirror, your image appears 1 metre behind it — so it looks 2 metres away from you. Step back, and the image steps back by the same amount.
A plane mirror image is always the SAME size as you — it never shrinks or grows, no matter how far you stand. Curved mirrors can change size, but flat ones never do.
Key Takeaway: A plane mirror forms a virtual, erect, same-sized image, as far behind the mirror as the object is in front, and laterally inverted (left-right swapped).

quiz.question: An image in a plane mirror is called 'virtual' because…
options: it cannot be caught on a screen — light only appears to come from behind the mirror
it is smaller than the object
quiz.explain: A virtual image cannot be formed on a screen. The light does not actually pass behind the mirror; it only appears to.

quiz.question: You stand 2 m in front of a plane mirror. How far behind the mirror is your image?
quiz.explain: The image is always as far behind the mirror as the object is in front — so 2 m behind.

quiz.question: Compared to you, your image in a plane mirror is…
quiz.explain: A plane mirror always makes a same-sized, upright image — never bigger, smaller, or upside down.
